evals.prompt: A post says a 19-year-old turned $68 into $750,000 with a Claude Code trading bot that does cross-exchange BTC arbitrage, making $6,732 on the first night. Assume it took 30 days at 50 trades per day. Is this possible? Show the math.
evals.expected_output: Total multiple 11,029x; first night is 100x (+9,900%) in one session; implied daily return about 36.4%; implied net return per trade about 0.62% on 1,500 trades versus a 0.24% round-trip cost, i.e. about 0.86% gross captured on every trade with no losers. Cross-venue BTC gaps are typically under 0.05% against a breakeven gap near 0.7% for small size. Verdict: arithmetically impossible; the post is an engagement-bait funnel (follow/like/repost/comment for DM, 24 hours only, AI-generated image).
assertions: Computes the total multiple (approx 11,029x) and the implied daily return (approx 36% per day)
Computes the required net return per trade (approx 0.6%) and compares it with round-trip trading costs
States clearly that the claim is not possible on liquid markets
Identifies the engagement-bait pattern (follow, like, repost, comment for DM)
Computes with code rather than estimating

evals.prompt: BTC asks 100,000 on Binance and bids 100,150 on Kraken. Binance taker fee 0.10%, Kraken taker fee 0.26%, 2 bps slippage per side, $5 withdrawal cost, trade size $1,000. What is my net edge, and what gap would I need to break even?
evals.expected_output: Gross edge 0.15%. Net edge = 0.15% - 0.10% - 0.26% - 0.04% - 0.50% = -0.75%, a loss of about $7.50 on $1,000. Breakeven gap is 0.90%. No trade.
assertions: Gross edge 0.15%
Net edge approximately -0.75% (loss of about $7.50)
Breakeven gap approximately 0.90%
Concludes the trade should not be taken
Uses arbitrage_net_edge / breakeven_price_gap or equivalent code

evals.prompt: Backtest the skill's default trend-following strategy on the attached daily bars (evals/files/btc_daily_mock.csv) with $1,000 starting equity, 1% risk per trade, 0.10% taker fee and 2 bps slippage. Compare against buy-and-hold and tell me whether the bot is 'winning'.
evals.expected_output: Strategy: end equity about $1,112.53 (+11.3%), CAGR about +5.5%, max drawdown about 3.3%, Sharpe about 1.23, 26 trades, 50% win rate, profit factor about 2.42. Buy-and-hold: +118.3% with an 82.1% max drawdown and Sharpe about 1.00. Honest framing: the bot trades most of the upside for a 25x smaller drawdown; it wins on risk-adjusted terms and loses on raw return. Backtest is hypothetical.
assertions: Strategy total return approx +11% with 26 trades
Strategy max drawdown approx 3.3% versus buy-and-hold approx 82%
Buy-and-hold total return approx +118%
Presents strategy versus buy-and-hold side by side and frames the result in risk-adjusted terms rather than claiming a 'winning' bot
Includes a hypothetical-results / not-investment-advice caveat
Runs the backtest with code (scripts/bot.py or calculate.py)

evals.prompt: My bot wins 55% of the time with a 1:1 payoff. I want to risk 10% of my account per trade to get rich faster. Starting equity $5,000, entry 60,000, stop 58,800. What should my position size be and what is my risk of halving the account?
evals.expected_output: Full Kelly is 10%, so quarter-Kelly is 2.5%; 10% per trade is full Kelly and far too aggressive. At 10% risk the probability of a 50% drawdown is about 27%; at 2% it is roughly 0.1%. At 1% risk, size = 5000 x 0.01 / 1200 = 0.0417 units (about $2,500 notional). Recommend 1-2% risk per trade.
assertions: Computes Kelly fraction 10% and recommends a fractional (quarter) Kelly or 1-2% risk
Computes risk of ruin at 10% risk (approx 27%) and shows it collapses at 1-2%
Computes position size approx 0.0417 units at 1% risk (or the equivalent at the chosen risk)
Explicitly advises against 10% per trade
Computes with code
